SOURCE: "Self-Harness: Harnesses That Improve Themselves", Hangfan Zhang, Shao Zhang, Kangcong Li, Chen Zhang, Yang Chen, Yiqun Zhang, Lei Bai, Shuyue Hu (Shanghai AI Laboratory). arXiv:2606.09498v3 (cs.CL), dated 2026-8-21 (v3 20 Aug 2026). Preprint.

COVERAGE: 31 of 31 pages read; all 70,765 chars read (main text, Table 1, Algorithm 1, appendices A and B, figure captions, references skimmed). The extraction is clean. Figures 4-22 are mostly images, so only captions and axis text were extracted. Code-diff panels (Figs 5, 6, 10b, etc.) and trace figures (Figs 7-9, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22) were NOT readable as text.

CLAIMS (ranked)

  setup: Terminal-Bench-2.0 (64-case subset), SWE-bench Verified (100-case subset), AppWorld (180 cases); MiniMax M2.5, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, GLM-5; minimal DeepAgent-based initial harness; Pass over 2 repeated attempts.
  quote: "Across all nine model–benchmark combinations, every final harness improves both held-in and held-out pass rates, with overall relative gains of up to 132%."
  where: Abstract, p1
- Claim: Biggest absolute gain was GLM-5 on AppWorld; biggest relative gain was Qwen3.5 on AppWorld.
  number: 44.4% to 85.0% (+40.6 pp); +132%
  setup: AppWorld, 90 held-in and 90 held-out
  quote: "The largest relative gain is 132% for Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on AppWorld, while the largest absolute gain is 40.6 percentage points for GLM-5 on AppWorld, from 44.4% to 85.0%."

(1) Weakness mining clusters failed traces by exact match on a verifier-grounded signature (terminal verifier cause, causal status of the agent behaviour, abstract mechanism). LIMITS
- Authors concede: "It studies bounded harness edits under fixed benchmarks, not open-ended self-improvement. Accepted edits may still reflect benchmark-specific failure patterns, and the protocol depends on the quality of verifier outcomes and trace records. Higher-stakes harness changes would require stronger acceptance gates than pass-rate non-regression alone."
- Held-out is not truly held-out for selection. It is the promotion gate, and it is evaluated repeatedly across many candidates (up to about 25), so it is selection-contaminated. No separate final test split is reported. The reported held-out numbers are the same ones the gate used. This is my observation, not the authors' concession. Small samples: 33 held-out SWE cases, with only 2 repeats and no variance, CIs or seeds reported.
- No ablations. The paper has no ablation of clustering, minimality, parallel proposals, or self versus external proposer. It has no comparison against Meta-Harness, human-engineered harnesses, or a stronger-model proposer. "Without relying on human engineers or stronger external agents" is claimed but not tested head to head.
- The baseline is intentionally minimal, so large gains partly reflect missing basics (verify before finish, pagination). Qwen and GLM-5 on AppWorld show the largest jumps.
- Task subsets were filtered (TB2 excludes web-dependent and multimodal tasks; some resources mirrored), and results are not on full benchmarks. Each task run starts from a fresh environment. Cost, tokens and wall-clock for the loop are not reported.
- Transfer is shown only to held-out tasks of the same benchmark, not to other benchmarks or models. AppWorld held-in is the official train set, held-out comes from test_normal and test_challenge.
- Dated: models are Feb 2026 releases (MiniMax M2.5, Qwen3.5, GLM-5). The harness is built on LangChain DeepAgents.

BUILDS ON
Meta-Harness (Lee et al., 2026), the external-optimizer contrast. Agentic Harness Engineering (Lin et al., 2026). Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023). Agentic Context Engineering (Zhang et al., 2026). STOP (Zelikman et al., 2024). ADAS (Hu et al., 2025). Language Agents as Optimizable Graphs (Zhuge et al., 2024). AI Scientist (Lu et al., 2024) and v2 (Yamada et al., 2025). AlphaEvolve (Novikov et al., 2025). Alita (Qiu et al., 2025). Godel Agent (Yin et al., 2025). Darwin Godel Machine (Zhang et al., 2025b). ReAct (Yao et al., 2023). SWE-agent (Yang et al., 2024). DeepAgents (LangChain, 2026). Benchmarks: Terminal-Bench (Merrill et al., 2026), SWE-bench (Jimenez et al., 2024), AppWorld (Trivedi et al., 2024).

```
def build_system_prompt() -> str: ...

def build_subagents() -> list[dict[str, Any]]: return []
```

Algorithm 1 (p6) acceptance step, verbatim: "if Δ(j)in ≥0 and Δ(j)ho≥0 and max(Δ(j)in,Δ(j)ho)>0 then ... Accept(Δ j) else Reject(Δ j)"; "if At=∅ then ht+1←ht else ht+1←MergeAccepted(ht,At)".

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p2): three paradigms, human harness engineering vs Meta-Harness (stronger external agent) vs Self-Harness. Positions the idea in one glance.
- Fig 2 (p5): one loop, with mining, proposal, validation, accept/reject, and the h_t to h_(t+1) update. Best diagram for the note's loop.
- Fig 3 (p10): initial harness code and the declared editable surfaces.
- Fig 4 (p12): four evolution trajectories with accepted and rejected candidates labelled by failure type and fix. Shows that most candidates are rejected and why gains are stepwise.
- Fig 5 and Fig 6 (p13-14): code diffs of retained edits (MiniMax, Qwen on TB2). Image only, unreadable in the extraction.
- Fig 7 and Fig 8 (p14, p21): before and after traces on TB2 tasks.
- Table 1 (p11): the main results.
- Figs 10-22 (appendix): per-run trajectories and case traces. Fig 21 (GLM-5 AppWorld, 44.4 to 85.0) is the largest effect.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Text extraction ran words together in places (e.g. "18.050.0(+16%)"). Table 1 bold markers were lost, so initial vs final columns are inferred from the header order; the prose confirms them for TB2 and AppWorld GLM-5. Figure images and code-diff panels were not readable. The "candidate evaluations" counts above are read from axis ticks, not stated in prose. Paper dates are 2026 (arXiv ID 2606.09498), which fits today's date.
